easy.explanation: Verse 1 says Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria.
easy.q: How many sons did Ahab have in Samaria?

answers: The rulers, elders, and those who brought up Ahab’s children
easy.explanation: Jehu wrote to the rulers, elders, and guardians of Ahab’s children.
easy.q: To whom did Jehu send letters?

easy.explanation: They took the king’s sons and slew seventy persons.
easy.q: What did the men of the city do to the king’s sons?

answers: Two kings had not been able to stand before him
medium.explanation: They said, “Behold, two kings stood not before him.”
medium.q: Why were the leaders of Samaria afraid of Jehu?

answers: That they crown one of Ahab’s sons
That they bring him the heads of the king’s sons
That they send him the king’s horses
medium.explanation: He commanded them to take the heads of their master’s sons to Jezreel.
medium.q: What did Jehu request in his second letter?

answers: Those who raised and cared for the royal children
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to those who brought up or raised Ahab’s children.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “the bringers up of the children” mean?

answers: As the fulfillment of the LORD’s word
As an order from the king of Judah
challenge.explanation: Jehu said that the LORD had done what He spoke by Elijah.
challenge.q: How did Jehu explain the destruction of Ahab’s house?

answers: They considered him more threatening than the two kings he had defeated
They trusted their army to defeat him
They immediately chose to fight him
challenge.explanation: They feared Jehu because two kings had already fallen before him.
challenge.q: What does the leaders’ response show about Jehu’s power?

answers: Only the city rulers were killed
All connected with Ahab’s house were destroyed, leaving none remaining
challenge.explanation: Jehu slew the great men, kinsfolks, priests, and all who remained.
challenge.q: How complete was Jehu’s destruction in Jezreel?

paragraphs.title: The Killing of Ahaziah’s Relatives and the Meeting with Jehonadab

easy.explanation: Jehu met the brethren of Ahaziah king of Judah.
easy.q: Whom did Jehu meet on the way to Samaria?

answers: To salute the children of the king and the queen
easy.explanation: They said they were going to salute the king’s children and the children of the queen.
easy.q: Why did Ahaziah’s brethren say they had come?

easy.explanation: Jehonadab son of Rechab came to meet Jehu.

medium.explanation: Jehu said, “Take them alive,” though they were then slain.
medium.q: What did Jehu command concerning Ahaziah’s brethren?

answers: He asked whether his heart was right with Jehu’s heart
He asked him to bring a sacrifice
medium.explanation: Jehu asked, “Is thine heart right, as my heart is with thy heart?”
medium.q: How did Jehu test Jehonadab’s loyalty?

answers: Are you loyal and of like purpose?
medium.explanation: Jehu was asking whether Jehonadab shared his purpose and loyalty.
medium.q: What does “Is thine heart right” mean here?

answers: Jehu regarded him as a close companion
challenge.explanation: Taking Jehonadab into the chariot showed fellowship in Jehu’s mission.
challenge.q: What is suggested by Jehu taking Jehonadab up into the chariot?

answers: Jehonadab became his companion in opposing Baal worship
challenge.explanation: Jehonadab went with Jehu and entered the house of Baal with him.
challenge.q: How did the meeting with Jehonadab relate to Jehu’s later actions?

answers: The destruction of those remaining from Ahab’s house
challenge.explanation: Jehu slew all that remained unto Ahab in Samaria.
challenge.q: What did Jehu complete in Samaria?

answers: Serve Baal more than Ahab did
easy.explanation: Jehu said, “Ahab served Baal a little; but Jehu shall serve him much.”
easy.q: What did Jehu claim he would do concerning Baal?

easy.explanation: He called all Baal’s prophets, servants, and priests.
easy.q: Whom did Jehu gather for the assembly?

easy.explanation: Jehu appointed fourscore, or eighty, men outside.
easy.q: How many men did Jehu station outside?

answers: To identify those attending the Baal assembly
medium.explanation: The vestments marked the worshippers gathered for Baal.
medium.q: Why were special garments provided for the Baal worshippers?

answers: That no servant of the LORD was present
That all Ahab’s sons had arrived
That the house of Baal was empty
medium.explanation: They were to make sure only Baal worshippers were there.
medium.q: What did Jehu require them to check before the action began?

medium.explanation: A solemn assembly is a formal gathering called for a special occasion.

answers: To gather Baal’s worshippers together so they could be destroyed
To persuade Jehonadab to worship Baal
challenge.explanation: Jehu used deceit to gather and destroy the worshippers of Baal.
challenge.q: What was the purpose of Jehu’s deception?

answers: So all of them would be gathered and none would escape the action
challenge.explanation: A complete gathering enabled Jehu to deal with all of them at once.
challenge.q: Why did Jehu insist that none of the Baal worshippers be missing?

challenge.explanation: They guarded the outside and were responsible for any person who escaped.
challenge.q: What was the purpose of the eighty men outside?

paragraphs.title: The Destruction of the Temple of Baal

answers: After the burnt offering was finished
easy.explanation: Jehu gave the command as soon as he had made an end of offering.
easy.q: When did Jehu command his men to begin killing?

easy.explanation: The guard and captains smote them with the edge of the sword.
easy.q: With what did Jehu’s men kill the worshippers?

easy.explanation: They brought out the images and burned them.
easy.q: What did they do with the images from Baal’s house?

answers: They broke it down and made it a draught house
They turned it into a palace
medium.explanation: They broke down the house and made it a place of refuse.
medium.q: What did they do to the house of Baal?

answers: The action was organized to prevent anyone from escaping
They came to join the worship
medium.explanation: Jehu commanded that none should come forth.
medium.q: What does the placement of the guard and captains show?

answers: Objects or statues used in pagan worship
medium.explanation: The images were pagan objects connected with Baal worship.
medium.q: What were the images in Baal’s house?

answers: Killing the worshippers, burning the images, breaking down the house, and making it a refuse place
Breaking down the house, inviting worshippers, and offering sacrifice
Burning the city, building a temple, and killing Jehu
challenge.explanation: This is the order described in verses 25–28.
challenge.q: What was the main sequence in the destruction of Baal’s house?

answers: It shows the complete removal and humiliation of the place of worship
It shows that it became a palace
challenge.explanation: The former temple was reduced to a place of refuse.
challenge.q: Why is it significant that the house of Baal became a draught house?

answers: Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel
The Baal worshippers fled to Judah
challenge.explanation: Verse 28 says, “Thus Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel.”
challenge.q: What overall result is stated at the end of the passage?

answers: The sins of Jeroboam and the golden calves
easy.explanation: Jehu departed not from Jeroboam’s sins and the golden calves.
easy.q: What form of idolatry did Jehu fail to remove?

easy.explanation: The LORD promised that Jehu’s children of the fourth generation would sit on Israel’s throne.
easy.q: To which generation was Jehu’s dynasty promised?

easy.explanation: Hazael smote Israel in all the coasts of Israel.
easy.q: Who smote Israel in all its coasts?

answers: Because he did well in executing what was right against Ahab’s house
Because he made peace with Syria
medium.explanation: The LORD said Jehu had done well in doing what was right in His eyes.
medium.q: Why was Jehu promised a continuing dynasty?

answers: He did not destroy Baal worship
He did not walk in the LORD’s law with all his heart and continued Jeroboam’s sins
medium.explanation: Though he destroyed Baal, Jehu continued in the sins of Jeroboam.
The phrase describes the beginning of Israel’s loss of territory.
medium.q: What does “to cut Israel short” mean in this context?

answers: He was commended and promised a dynasty for destroying Baal, yet Israel suffered because he continued Jeroboam’s sins
He failed in everything he did
He served Baal but destroyed the golden calves
challenge.explanation: The passage records both Jehu’s obedience against Ahab and his failure to follow the LORD fully.
challenge.q: How are Jehu’s achievements and sins presented together?

answers: The land east of Jordan, including Gilead, Gad, Reuben, and Manasseh
challenge.explanation: The passage lists Gilead and the territories east of Jordan.
challenge.q: Which region came under Hazael’s attack?

answers: Israel began losing territory while Jehu continued those sins
The sins caused Jehu to enlarge Israel’s borders
The passage does not mention lost territory
challenge.explanation: After describing Jehu’s continued sins, the text describes Israel being cut short.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between Jeroboam’s sins and Israel’s condition?

easy.explanation: Jehoahaz his son reigned in his stead.
Jehu reigned twenty and eight years.
easy.q: How long did Jehu reign over Israel?

answers: The book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel
The chronicles of the kings of Judah only
medium.explanation: The text refers to the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
medium.q: Where does the text direct readers for more information about Jehu?

answers: Jehu was buried, and his son Jehoahaz reigned in his stead
Jehoahaz was buried, and Jehu returned to the throne
medium.explanation: After Jehu’s death and burial, Jehoahaz became king.
medium.q: What was the succession at the end of the passage?

medium.explanation: The expression refers to Jehu’s death, followed by his burial.
medium.q: What does “slept with his fathers” mean here?

answers: Another source recorded Jehu’s acts and might
Nothing was known about Jehu’s reign
challenge.explanation: The text points to another record containing the rest of Jehu’s acts and might.
challenge.q: What does the reference to the chronicles of the kings of Israel indicate?

answers: The exact length is stated: twenty-eight years
challenge.explanation: The final verse explicitly gives the length of his reign.
challenge.q: Which detail emphasizes the length of Jehu’s reign?

answers: Jehu’s death leads to the reign of his son Jehoahaz
challenge.explanation: Jehoahaz succeeded Jehu after his burial.
challenge.q: How does the ending connect with Jehu’s dynasty?
